The actual b0(c) of CMP109 p267 for the positive coarse edge c=(j,mu) has fine initial index i_mu=L j_mu+L-1 and i_nu=L j_nu+h for nu!=mu; its terminal index is i+e_mu. BLOCK COMPATIBILITY. A regular continuous cube of side S eta, S=L^s, s>=1, with corners at S eta integer coordinates is exactly a union of physical first-block cells. Its fine center indices in each interval are Sa,...,S(a+1)-1. Its coarse center indices are (S/L)a,...,(S/L)(a+1)-1; S/L is odd. Therefore any compatible union X of these cubes satisfies: y in X on the coarse lattice implies B(y) subset X on the fine lattice. Unions, intersections, complements and erosions by whole cells preserve this property. Apply this only to the source-compatible Omega1, not arbitrary subsets or old anchored auxiliary gauge blocks.

INCIDENCE. For such X, an incident fine link interval intersects X iff at least one fine endpoint lies in X. The link visits just the two adjacent fine cells, whose center sets are disjoint from all region faces. The analogous statement holds for the coarse lattice because X is a union of coarse cells. Thus if I=E_coarse(X) uses independent positive incident coarse rows, every c in I has one coarse endpoint y in X. The corresponding pivot endpoint lies in B(y) subset X. Consequently beta(c) belongs to E_fine(X), including coarse crossing rows. This proves injective membership for interior and crossing rows on that specified geometry; purely exterior rows are not in I.

TYPED COMPLEMENT GATE. If, and only for this argument if, the original prescribed fine set is F=E_total minus E_fine(X), all these original beta(c) are outside F. Under this same convention a purely exterior coarse row, whose two blocks are outside X, uses only exterior fine links along its endpoint paths and translated straight paths; it depends on V0 only. This is the structural split compatible with the retained exterior coarse delta in CMP119(1.15). It does not by itself prove a pointwise conditional integral, any normalizer or nonzero denominator.

It would belong to that alternate exterior and hence be fixed.
